synopsis: ISO 21815-1:2022 provides off-road collision-warning and avoidance test procedures; clause 6 specifies physical test environments, surfaces, machine conditions, objects, pass/fail performance tests and false-positive tests [f5156, f5353, f7726]. Complementary methods include ISO 16001:2017 for detection bodies, zones and times, ISO 3450:2011 for braking, and ISO 17757:2019 for testing in manual and autonomous modes; ISO 3450 prescribes adverse braking configurations and maximum payload for dumpers [f5155, f10651, f8938, f13623]. The review found neither a complete numeric regulatory type-approval test for off-road automatic braking nor an off-road Euro NCAP equivalent, and it did not establish universal target dimensions, test counts or acceptance of simulation evidence [f2147, f346, f5410, f11192]. South African mining published independent verification specifications on 29 August 2025, with industry specifications written in 2025 and 2026; the published closed-loop specification uses unloaded machines and gradients of 1 percent or less, while the regulation itself supplies no detection percentage, false-alarm limit or stopping test [f348, f11459, f13715, f165]. Heavy-truck precedents show why passenger-car tests should not be copied directly: stopping distances and towing equipment required adaptations, and Daimler disputed the real-world relevance of a steel-trench-plate reproduction scenario [f1232, f1233, f1314]. Reproducible product tests also leave operational limitations: static tests miss speed-dependent detection effects, and ISO tests cannot predict a fatigued operator's response to repeated nuisance warnings [f10656, f3494].
